Based on the healthcare Q&A matches, it appears that preventing osteoporosis may be a contributing factor to reducing aromatase inhibitor (AI)-related musculoskeletal symptoms. Patients on AIs who develop osteoporosis are at increased risk of musculoskeletal symptoms and bone fractures. Comedic relief with Ca/Bis can help reduce the likelihood of osteoporosis, while patients who received tamoxifen before starting AI therapy were less likely to develop AI-related musculoskeletal symptoms.

To eliminate these symptoms, it is recommended that patients on AIs should be offered Ca/Bis to reduce the incidence of musculoskeletal symptoms and fracture. Additionally, patients on AIs may benefit from being assessed for osteoporosis and receiving treatment as necessary to prevent or manage osteoporosis.

While there are other factors contributing to AI-related musculoskeletal symptoms, preventing osteoporosis is a key consideration in managing these symptoms.
